subject: home-economics
summary: Short Section A cards with one answer per row (true/false, fabric properties) look clean and are easy to mark on both phone and desktop. The serious faults are in the scheme and the attachment. Where the student picks from a pool of options, the whole pool is pasted as one grey paragraph under EVERY criterion, so the same wall of text repeats six times on the floor-coverings card (about five phone screens) and six times on the flour card, with author working notes such as 'the source gives no separate name tariff', 'no models are invented' and 'Complete historical cell wording' shown to the student. Every one of the 8 attached 'Source and question' pages failed with 'That page did not load', so no attachment could be judged. Two questions that are answer tables on the paper are flattened (raw pipe header on the iron card) or shown only as a tiny picture on the phone.

issues.title: Attached page fails to load on every card that has one
issues.detail: All 8 cards whose manifest lists sourceMaterial (1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11) open a reader that shows only 'That page did not load. You can retry or open the original examination document.' with a Try again button. The header and footer render (PDF PAGE n, paper credit) but the page image never appears. The button on the card promises '1 printed page · exact examination text'. Because nothing loaded, whether the page is limited to this question could not be checked. Cards 2, 4, 9 and 12 have no sourceMaterial in the manifest and correctly show no attachment button.
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the page asset/URL for Home Economics question pages (it fails for 2010 through 2026, both levels, so it is subject-wide, not one paper). Until it works, hide the button rather than show a dead reader. Card 8 needs it most: the stem says 'Shown below is the ground floor plan of a house' and nothing is shown.

issues.title: Whole answer pool repeated as a wall of text under every criterion
issues.detail: Card 1: each of the six criteria (Description and properties for coverings 1, 2, 3) carries the same ~300-word run of every floor covering in the scheme, separated by ' | ' and semicolons ('Description: Ceramic tiles - made of water, clay and minerals; ... | Description: Flagstone/cut stone ...'). The phone card is five columns long and the desktop page is cut off after the third repeat. Card 8: the full architect/surveyor/engineer/solicitor/builder text repeats under both 'Name' criteria. Card 3: the flattened table 'Type of flour Culinary use 1. wholemeal /wheat meal / brown 1. brown bread / scones 2. white / plain / cream 2. pastry, bread...' repeats six times with flour names and uses interleaved. Card 11: seven agencies and their details run together with no breaks ('...creating more employment County Enterprise Board offers support... jobs FÁS/ Solas –community...'). Card 9: a 20-mark answer is one grey paragraph.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the pool ONCE, as a list or table: one row per floor covering with Description and Properties columns (card 1), a two-column Type of flour / Culinary use table (card 3), one titled block per professional or agency (cards 8, 11), one block per nutrient (card 9). Put the per-criterion mark buttons after it with a one-line label only. For cards 1 and 3 a crop of the official scheme table would be clearer than the text.

issues.title: Author working notes shown to the student as scheme text
issues.detail: Internal commentary appears in the scheme: 'the source gives no separate name tariff and no internal description split. Complete original paired models:' and 'no models are invented' (card 1); 'Complete historical cell wording:' and 'description graded 2:0. Clarification: ... The categories are not simply synonyms for ferrous and ferric.' (card 2); 'Complete printed table:' (card 3); 'Complete guidance:' (cards 4, 6); 'The scheme prints 6 marks for the complete question, with no per-answer allocation or partial-credit ladder ... no separate answer marks have been inferred' inside a tick box (card 5); 'Select Professional service 1 of 2 DIFFERENT options, keeping the SAME option throughout its criteria ... no description model is invented' (card 8); 'the scheme’s “lacto-vegetarians” wording is inaccurate. Complete historical guidance:' (card 9); 'Original historical source:' (card 11). Mark scales are written as ratios, 'graded 3:2:0', '4:3:2:1:0'.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the provenance notes from the student view. Replace ratio shorthand with plain words ('3 marks for a full point, 2 for a partial one'). In card 5 the first tick box should read just 'Water-soluble — e.g. B, C'.

issues.title: Answer-table questions flattened or shown only as a tiny picture
issues.detail: Card 2 opens with a raw header line 'Form of iron | Description | Food source Haem iron Non-haem iron' (pipe characters), then the question, then the rows again as 'Haem iron: description; food source'. Cards 3 and 5 show the question ONLY as a crop of the paper; on the phone its text is roughly a third the height of the app's body text and unreadable without Enlarge, and the crop is mostly an empty answer grid. Card 10 runs the three properties together and leaves the picture credit in the sentence: 'Explain each of the following fabric properties. (www.textilelearner.net) Absorbent Flammable Crease resistant'.
issues.suggested_fix: Always give the question as text in the app's own type ('Name three types of flour used in home baking and give one different culinary use of each.') and drop the empty-table crop. Card 2: delete the pipe header line. Card 10: list the three properties as bullets and remove the URL.

issues.title: Duplicate picture in the question area
issues.detail: Card 4 shows the dress/suit photo twice: once large under the quotation, then again smaller in a second crop that also repeats the quotation, the '(i)' label and the question text. Two Enlarge buttons and two credit lines follow. The second crop is cut off at 'Refer to:'.

issues.title: Criterion labels and mark controls are vague
issues.detail: Criterion headings are lowercase fragments ('properties', 'guidelines', 'causes', 'nutritional significance') with generic 'Point 1 / Point 2' rows and a monospace '0m of 6m' counter. Card 7's scheme is a single line of terse fragments ('Geographical location; foreign/global competition; low incentive...') for a 9-mark 'Discuss' question, which is what the scheme prints but gives the student little to check against. Card 11 has a clear 'Name: one of these' pick list, but ticking the name and then scoring 'Details' 0 or 5 with no part marks is abrupt.
issues.suggested_fix: Capitalise and phrase the heading as the task ('Three guidelines, 2 marks each'); show the acceptable points as a bulleted list.

good_examples.why: Statements listed one per line; scheme gives each statement with True/False and a simple 0/2 control.
Scheme states each property with its meaning in one bold line and a 0/1/2 control; fits one phone screen (question line needs tidying).
Photo is large and legible and the scheme is split under the three headings the question asks for (apart from the duplicated image).
